podcast.title: Balancing Music and Nursing
podcast.body: Hurst had to quit his nursing position when Econoline Crush became seriously reactivated, but he still expresses a love for the work and indicates he might return to it, acknowledging that "the music thing just can't last forever." "When a car line crush was seriously reactivated and started getting back to work, Trevor had to quit his nurse gig."

podcast.title: Documentary Subject
podcast.body: Trevor Hurst's experience working in the Kenna Poaca indigenous community is documented in a film called "Flatlander." "A documentary called Flatlander covers his experience."

podcast.title: Return to Education for Psychiatric Nursing
podcast.body: After Econoline Crush's initial breakup and sporadic returns, Trevor Hurst, at age 45, enrolled in a psychiatric nursing program at Brandon University in 2011. This decision was driven by financial needs (having four kids), an interest in psychology, and his personal history with alcohol and addiction demons. "So in 2011, Trevor went back to school at the age of 45."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Work in Indigenous Community
podcast.body: After graduating, Hurst found a job at Kenna Poaca, a Dakota community in southwest Manitoba, which had sought help for two years. He became deeply involved in the community's indigenous culture for several years, also serving as an instructor for nursing fundamentals. "Trevor became deeply involved in the community's indigenous culture, spending several years there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: Trevor Hurst has been the sole constant member of Econoline Crush, with almost three dozen other musicians having been part of the band at various times. "Singer Trevor Hurst has been the only constant member of Econoline Crush. There are almost three dozen former members."

xref.title: Trevor Hurst's Nursing Career and Personal Journey
xref.body: Trevor Hurst embarked on a new career as a nurse, earning his nursing degree from Brand New University at the age of 45. He has worked in Manitoba First Nations Reserves, assisting with addiction, after overcoming his own issues with alcohol by attending AA. "Trevor has a new gig as a nurse. He spent time in places like Manitoba First Nations Reserves helping people deal with addiction."

xref.title: Vancouver Origins and Career Arc
xref.body: Econoline Crush emerged from Vancouver in the early 1990s, led by frontman Trevor Hurst. They had a solid 10-year run before initially breaking up in 2002, but later returned in 2006 to record and perform sporadically, eventually reactivating more seriously. "Econoline Crush came out of Vancouver in the early 1990s, headed up by frontman Trevor Hurst."
